subject.title: [Feature]: Auto-discovery of agent configurations from external workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw add core trusted workspace-agent discovery, or keep agent registration explicit through existing config/RPC workflows?
rationale: The request adds new config, filesystem scanning, trust boundaries, and live routing semantics that repository policy treats as product/security decisions, not a strict bug fix.

options.title: Keep Explicit Registration
options.body: Preserve `agents.list`, `$include`, and `agents.create/update/delete` as the canonical path, and improve zero-restart explicit registration before adding glob-based discovery.

options.title: Design Trusted Discovery
options.body: Accept the feature direction only after specifying trusted roots, config precedence, validation, reload semantics, and security proof.

options.title: Defer To External Tooling
options.body: Document script/operator generation patterns around current config APIs and close core discovery unless a smaller missing API is identified.

recommendation.title: Keep Explicit Registration
recommendation.body: Preserve `agents.list`, `$include`, and `agents.create/update/delete` as the canonical path, and improve zero-restart explicit registration before adding glob-based discovery.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest current source-history signal on the central agent config and gateway agent-management paths.
